items.title: Go-Live Is Not Success: Validation and Testing in Logistics Transformation
items.description: A logistics transformation can be technically successful and operationally disappointing. That happens when the implementation team proves that the system was built correctly but nobody proves that it improved the logistics outcome the business funded it to improve. The post Go-Live Is Not Success: Validation and Testing in Logistics Transformation appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
A logistics transformation can be technically successful and operationally disappointing. That happens when the implementation team proves that the system was built correctly but nobody proves that it improved the logistics outcome the business funded it to improve.
Systems engineering separates two ideas that logistics programs should take more seriously: verification and validation. Verification asks whether the system was built correctly. Validation asks whether the right system was built. The move toward the Autonomous Logistics Network raises the validation burden rather than reducing it, because greater machine authority increases the consequence of untested assumptions and failure paths.
A new TMS can calculate routes correctly and still fail to improve transportation performance. A WMS can execute transactions correctly and still fail to improve order cycle time. A control tower can display every exception and still fail to reduce decision latency.
A warehouse automation system can operate exactly as specified and still create a bottleneck somewhere else in the building. A control tower can ingest all required data and still fail to reduce decision latency. An AI model can be accurate and still produce recommendations that users cannot execute.
These systems may pass technical tests. They have not necessarily passed the business test.
Validation returns to the original requirements. Did the new system improve the outcome it was designed to improve? Does it perform under realistic operating conditions? Do people use it as intended? Does it work across interfaces and exceptions, not just inside the core application?
That is the standard transformation should meet.
Technology projects naturally test components. Logistics networks need end-to-end tests.
A customer order should be able to move through allocation, warehouse, yard, transportation, delivery, and customer-service processes. A carrier-capacity disruption should trigger the expected information flow and decision response. A route, cutoff, or priority change should reach execution in time to matter.
The test is not whether each system processed its transaction. The test is whether the total operating flow produced the intended result.

Google's AI search problem finally shows up in the earnings report, some investors believe
Google 三季度搜索收入增长约 12%，低于分析师预期的 15%，市值一度缩水最多 10%。高管 Philipp Schindler 承认 AI mode 查询的强劲增长因变现率较低产生了影响，同时公司称搜索查询年增速达五年来最高，并计划在美国及国际市场扩大聊天机器人广告项目。
文章把 Google 财报数据与 AI 搜索变现压力联系起来，读者可以借此核对市场担忧与官方说法之间的差距。
第三季度搜索收入增长约12%，低于分析师预期的15%，这一缺口或许指向谷歌核心业务的某种紧张关系。AI驱动的搜索查询增长迅速，但带来的收入仍少于传统搜索。
谷歌在财报电话会上部分证实了这一点。高管Philipp Schindler表示，“AI模式查询的强劲增长因变现率较低而产生了影响”，此外还有其他因素。不过公司仍表示对整体走势满意，并称搜索查询的年增长率达到五年来最高水平。
而部分真相是，传统搜索多年来一直被宣告死亡，却始终在增长。本季度增速略低于预期，但与近年水平一致，而且谷歌才刚刚开始对AI模式变现。电话会上，公司宣布计划在美国及国际市场扩大其聊天机器人广告项目。
CEO Sundar Pichai表示，Gemini应用用户已达10亿，成为公司历史上增长最快的产品。这并不令人意外，因为它本质上只是搜索的附加功能，而搜索本身规模已经极其庞大。谷歌自家模型的API每分钟处理近320亿个token，是一年前的四倍多。这一跃升部分可能反映的是 推理模型和智能体工作流带来的token膨胀 ，而不只是使用量增加。
云部门同比增长103%，达到307亿美元，谷歌的支出也相应跟上。仅第三季度资本支出就达514亿美元。2026年全年预测维持在1950亿至2050亿美元，2027年预计将“显著更高”。
云业务负责人Thomas Kurian预计，AI智能体将推动云业务进一步增长，因为投入生产的智能体越多，其任务需要越多算力、智能体记忆需要越多存储、推理需要越多数据库容量。
谷歌有望在两端受益：既通过自家消费产品，也通过其他公司运行所依赖的基础设施。Pichai表示，公司正在构建 新Carbon模型 的更小蒸馏版本，以平衡质量与响应速度，并计划通过常开的云端运行时向“数十亿”用户提供服务。完整的Carbon模型初期只会提供给部分网络安全专家和美国政府。

items.title: OpenAI 详解如何检测前沿模型失准行为
items.description: OpenAI 发布长文，详解其针对前沿模型失准行为的多层监测系统，包括激活探针、基于模型的审查、调查智能体和自动化调查四层架构，并对 GPT‑6 Astra 及以上模型的全部 RL 运行、评估和内部 Codex 流量进行监测。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ck2bk0ns12i2hkg4ae0eoeabv
items.excerpt:
How we detect frontier model misalignment
OpenAI 发布长文，详解其针对前沿模型失准行为的多层监测系统，包括激活探针、基于模型的审查、调查智能体和自动化调查四层架构，并对 GPT‑6 Astra 及以上模型的全部 RL 运行、评估和内部 Codex 流量进行监测。
原文详述了 OpenAI 多层失准监测系统的架构与真实响应案例，读者可以了解其覆盖范围、误报处理和独立红队测试结果。
随着我们训练能力越来越强的 AI 模型，我们需要可靠的方法来检测它们的行为何时偏离了我们的预期。智能体可能在训练、评估或部署期间行为失当、采取未经授权的操作，后果可能很严重。为了发现这些故障，并在必要时及时干预，我们会监控智能体的推理过程、所采取的操作，以及这些操作如何影响其环境。
我们 监控内部编程智能体 已有一段时间，但 Hugging Face 事件 暴露出我们覆盖范围中的一个缺口：该事件始于内部网络安全评估，而当时我们并未对这些评估运行失准行为监控。针对这起事件，也考虑到我们的模型 能力日益增强 这一更广泛的背景，我们大幅扩展了监控智能体行为的系统。我们的失准监控现在覆盖前沿模型在更多种场景下的表现，包括训练、评估、内部使用，以及外部部署（具体会根据产品场景做相应调整）。
为了看清这套扩展后的系统本可以如何帮助阻止 Hugging Face 事件，我们用强化后的监控重放了该事件中记录的行为。在那次模拟中，监控系统在智能体首次逃出沙箱约 30 分钟后向安全团队发出警报——比实际事件中 Hugging Face 系统被攻破早了 30 多个小时。我们认为，这一预警本可以让响应人员有足够时间在模型能够访问外部服务之前很早就中断相关活动。
今年 9 月，我们看到了响应人员如何利用一次实时训练运行中的警报。一个模型找到了从本应隔离的环境中 接入互联网⁠（在新窗口打开） 的方法。我们的监控在 15 分钟内标记了这次突破，响应人员三分钟后就着手审查。随后我们暂停了前沿强化学习，同时加固用于约束智能体的系统。
这套监控系统需要消耗大量算力，但我们认为，随着模型能力增强、模型失准的潜在后果加重，这笔成本值得付出。监控是我们 纵深防御 策略的若干层之一，用于防范失准模型行为带来的危害。对齐训练旨在降低模型做出有害行为的倾向；安全控制 限制智能体能够访问或影响的系统 ；而当这些防护措施失效时，监控帮助我们检测残留的故障、在危害发生前干预，并从出错之处吸取教训。我们认为， 所有模型开发者 都应监控其能力最强的模型的行为。
对于能力至少与 GPT‑6 Astra 相当的模型，我们会监控每一次强化学习（RL）运行和评估，以及任何支持工具使用的测试框架。对于大多数工作负载（包括 RL 和评估），我们还会监控那些我们评估为能力超过 GPT‑5.5 Thinking 的模型。此外，无论使用哪个模型，所有内部 Codex 流量都在我们的监控范围内。这套系统还有一个版本，会按照我们在 准备框架 中设定的网络安全能力“临界”阈值，对超过该阈值的模型的外部工具使用进行监控，具体见下文。
为了在高效利用算力的同时发现事件，我们把监控系统设计成多层架构。前几层筛选阶段投入的算力相对较少，目标是尽可能多地筛出可疑案例：这些阶段的设计原则是宁可放行，即使证据模棱两可。后面的层则可以在每个案例上投入更多算力，弄清发生了什么、模型的行为是否值得担忧、以及是否需要干预。
最初一层（L0）使用我们称为 激活探针 的轻量级分类器。它们会在模型的内部激活中寻找可疑模式，并把标记出的案例交给下一层复核。我们把这些探针调向高召回率，宁可接受一些误报，也要降低漏掉可疑行为的可能。
由于我们仍在评估这些探针检测不熟悉的对齐偏差形式的效果，我们还会把探针未标记的流量中随机 5% 送到下一层。复核这部分样本，有助于我们发现探针可能漏掉的可疑行为。考虑到探针的敏感度，我们让前沿 RL 运行和内部 Codex 流量跳过这一层，直接进入下一层。
在下一层（L1），一个基于模型的审查器会检查智能体近期的对话、思维链和工具使用情况，寻找欺骗、未经授权的操作以及试图操纵评估的迹象。审查器使用的是智能体行动时所拥有的同一个上下文窗口。如果智能体早先的工作已被摘要压缩进待审查的上下文窗口，审查器看到的就是那份摘要。
对于前沿 RL 运行和内部 Codex 流量，我们在每一轮结束时运行一次 L1 检查，并在智能体为腾出上下文窗口空间而摘要其早先工作时也运行一次。我们目前正转向一种新安排：两次检查之间的间隔不超过 30 分钟。
一旦知道智能体被要求做什么，它的行为看起来可能大不相同。当 L1 审查器标记出某个案例时，该案例会被送到下一层（L2），由我们的调查智能体进一步检查。这个调查智能体可以核查评估的目的，并且在完整记录可用时，回读智能体所有的上下文窗口，弄清它是如何做出这些行动的。调查智能体还能在隔离环境中编写并运行代码来检查相关证据，然后利用发现的结果还原事件经过、识别重复报告，并判断该案例的严重程度。
我们针对不同目的使用不同的调查智能体。安全调查智能体负责寻找可能需要人工介入的迹象，比如智能体逃出沙箱或未经授权访问系统。对齐调查智能体则负责寻找值得研究的行为，即便这些行为没有直接的安全风险。在两类调查智能体同时启用的场景下，每个被 L1 层标记的案例都会由两者分别审查。我们目前正在把对齐调查推广到更多内部工作负载中。
对于敏感工作负载，包括内部 Codex 使用、评估和强化学习运行，下一层（L3）会做进一步检查，依据的是对话之外的证据。安全调查智能体会把对话记录与网络日志、其他系统遥测数据以及以往案例的证据进行比对，据此判断是否需要通知人工响应人员。在 L3，对齐审查人员还会跨案例比对报告，找出严重故障和反复出现的模式，并对前沿强化学习运行做更深入的检查。

【X 长文】You're probably overprompting Claude
Newer models require less prompting than most of us still do.
For Opus 5.5, try giving Claude a single prompt with a clear goal of what you want to do and how Claude should verify it has achieved it, and let Claude work on it. Start with /effort medium and adjust as needed.
If you don't know yet what you're trying to do, ask Claude to interview you until it could write a spec. Then start a new session and use that spec to build what you want.
Claude will stop on its own when it believes it's done.
If it can execute something that checks in terms of pass/fail or a number to beat, with reports in a way it can read, Claude can keep going without you having to watch.
For long background tasks, you can use /goal to specify a condition that a separate model to check after every turn.
Recent versions of Claude Code have also adopted auto mode as the default starting mode for interactive terminal sessions. In that mode, a classifier analyzes Claude's actions rather than relying on the usual permission prompts. This is not a guarantee of safe behavior - neither is blindly approving every prompt. When Claude reports back, ask it to show you the command and output or a screenshot.
For models like Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5, over 80% of the Claude Code system prompt was removed with no measurable degradation of its coding evals.
When a new model like Opus 5.5 comes out, you can do the same experiment with your own instructions: remove some, then add back only those that the model misses. The /doctor prompt-audit command flags those written for older models.
Another area to reduce your own work is subagents.
Claude delegates to them on its own, so you rarely need to ask. Ask only for substantial, standalone work like long audits or migrations, which Opus 5.5 can split across parallel subagents. An initiative bringing together universities, research organizations, industry, and the open science community to make publicly funded research easier to discover, reuse, and build upon.
Today, we're announcing Project ProtoStar , an initiative to unlock the potential of publicly funded scientific research by making datasets, models, and code more accessible and reusable, particularly for AI-driven research. ProtoStar brings together research institutions, industry, and the open science community to support the release of scientific artifacts in AI-ready, machine-actionable formats, and to demonstrate their value through a series of open challenges. The first challenge, hosted by Carnegie Mellon University , opens on November 2. See How to Participate below.
The initiative's founding partners include Carnegie Mellon University , Purdue University , Georgia Institute of Technology , Arizona State University , and The George Washington University , all working through the Open Forum for AI (OFAI) as the university coalition partner; the Astera Institute ; Hugging Face as the infrastructure partner; and the Open Research Community Accelerator (ORCA) , through its Fostering Innovation Network , as the community partner.
Participating organizations formalize their involvement through a memorandum of understanding supporting the release of suitable scientific datasets, models, and code in AI-ready formats on open infrastructure. Organizations interested in joining Project ProtoStar can reach out to protostar@orcaopen.org .
The U.S. federal government invests approximately $190 billion annually in research and development , and federal policy increasingly expects the results to be shared publicly. items.excerpt:
Mistral Large 4 (aka Le Chonk) is a multimodal, multilingual, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model from Mistral. It takes text and images as input and generates text. It has about 1T total, 49B active parameter , and a context window of 1M tokens .
The model is released in two official variants:
There are also GGUFs created by Unsloth and the llama.cpp team. It’s distributed under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License (an MIT derivative that establishes limitations for model-as-a-service offerings).
Mistral Large 4 is particularly strong for cybersecurity, coding agents, and multimodality. In this post, we look at how the model works, its capabilities, architecture and more!
Mistral Large 4 combines a large pool of experts with sparse attention and a Pixtral vision encoder. The language model selects a small group of experts for each token, while its attention indexer selects which earlier token positions to attend to. These are two different forms of sparsity, where one selects feed-forward networks, the other selects context positions.
You can find all the checkpoints in the Mistral Large 4 collection .
Mistral Large 4 scores 82% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index test that asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch the software. Mistral reports that several closed frontier models score near zero on the same test because they refuse to attempt the work. This is super important for defenders, because fixing a vulnerability usually requires reproducing the vulnerability. In Mistral’s internal testing, Mistral Large 4 was also useful for malware analysis, vulnerability prioritisation and writing detection rules, which the model was not explicitly trained for.
Mistral mainly positions the model for defensive security work. Vulnerability research and incident response often appear like attacks in model input, so closed source filters can block them. A team that depends on an API can also lose access in the middle of an incident. Crucially, open weight models put both the usage policy and the deployment under the user’s control. That said, the model still declines harmful requests: on cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm, its average refusal rate is higher than any other open weight model.

items.excerpt:
Language models can do a lot. They write, summarize, translate, and call tools. But they're only a small part of what machine learning can do.
Say a customer calls your support line. First, you want to know what they said (speech recognition). Then, you want to decide where to send them (decision). You could hand both to a language model, but there are models built for each that are better, faster, and less expensive.
In our AnyLanguageModel 1.0 recap , we looked at a year of local and hosted models in Swift. With AnyLanguageModel and swift-huggingface now on their 1.x releases, we're extending the same approach to speech and decisions: familiar Swift APIs with a choice of model.
Both packages can download open models from the Hugging Face Hub and run them on device.
Computers have been transcribing speech for decades, and in the past few years, they've gotten very good at it. Apple platforms already have an API for it. macOS 26 and iOS 26 introduced SpeechAnalyzer , Apple's new speech-to-text API. You add modules such as SpeechTranscriber and SpeechDetector to an analyzer, give it a file or a stream of audio buffers, and read results from async sequences as they arrive. AssetInventory installs the models, so your app decides when downloads happen.
It's a well-designed API, but the only engine behind it is Apple's. AnySpeechRecognizer keeps the API and lets you choose the engine:
The package mirrors SpeechAnalyzer , SpeechTranscriber , DictationTranscriber , SpeechDetector , and AssetInventory , with Apple's Speech framework as the default engine. Parakeet Unified is NVIDIA's English-only Parakeet .

items.excerpt:
Day 0 support for Mistral Large 4 on vLLM
vLLM 团队宣布对 Mistral 新旗舰模型 Mistral Large 4 提供 Day 0 支持，该模型为 1T 参数、每 token 激活 49B 的原生多模态 MoE 模型，采用 MLA 稀疏注意力加 DSA top-k 索引器、跨层 KV 共享、NoPE、SSMax 和 LeRoPE 等新架构，并内置 DSpark 推测解码草稿器与 Pixtral 视觉编码器。
vLLM 团队详解支持 Mistral Large 4 所需的架构适配与量化、长上下文、推测解码等实测数据，可作部署参考。
我们很高兴地宣布，vLLM 已实现 Mistral Large 4 的 day-0 支持。Mistral Large 4 是 Mistral 推出的新一代前沿混合专家（MoE）原生多模态模型。它把 DeepSeek 风格的稀疏注意力栈（MLA 加 DSA top-k 索引器）与多项新架构特性结合在一起：跨层 KV 共享、NoPE 层、SSMax 和 LeRoPE。模型自带 DSpark 投机解码草稿器和 Pixtral 视觉编码器。
支持它远不止加一个模型文件那么简单。ML4 运行在 vLLM 的模型运行器 V2（MRV2）上，并支持可断开的 CUDA 图。它的各个构建模块放在新的 vllm/models/mistral/ 包中，这项工作还顺带改进了 decode 上下文并行（DCP）、prefill 上下文并行（PCP）、DSpark、基于 NIXL 的分离式服务以及 HiSparse 主机内存 KV 卸载。
Mistral Large 4 的支持包含在 vllm/vllm-openai:mistral-large-4 Docker 镜像中，该镜像还包含 mistral-common 1.13。下面的命令在镜像内运行 vllm serve ：
4 块 GPU 上的 NVFP4 （Blackwell；在 8 块 GPU 上使用 --tensor-parallel-size 8 ）：
NVFP4 不以质量换速度。在多模态、长上下文、智能体编程、业务自动化和网络安全评测中，它在每项任务上与 FP8 的差距都在 2.1 分以内，平均差异为 −0.3 分。token 消耗也相当：平均补全 token 数与 FP8 相差约 4% 以内。它还更快、更省：在 TP8 下，不使用投机解码时 NVFP4 每 token 解码速度比 FP8 快 1.08–1.19 倍（启用 DSpark 时为 1.18–1.22 倍），KV 缓存容量约为 1.5 倍。
*FP8 与 NVFP4 在核心评测上的得分和 token 消耗对比。误差条为通过自助法估计的 95% 置信区间。在所有领域，包括多模态推理（GDP.pdf、MathVision）、长上下文（Graphwalks 512k）、编程智能体（DeepSWE、SWE-bench Pro、Terminal-Bench 4）、业务自动化（AutomationBench）和网络安全（CyberGym），NVFP4 检查点的表现都与 FP8 一致。
长上下文（DCP）。 添加 --decode-context-parallel-size 8 可将潜在 KV 缓存分片到 8 个 rank 上。这要求使用默认的 FP8 KV 缓存。
多模态。 传入 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": N}' 可允许每个提示词最多 N 张图片。
多节点、分离式 P/D 以及其他已测试的配置，参见 Mistral Large 4 配方 。
*72 个解码器层：每第 4 层为 NoPE，28 层复用最近的前一个 indexer 层的 top-k，NoPE 层 39–71 读取第 35 层的 latent KV，且只有第 0 层是稠密层。*
稀疏 MLA + DSA indexer。 ML4 复用了 vLLM 的稀疏 MLA 栈（带 fp8_ds_mla latent cache 的 FlashMLA 稀疏实现，外加带 FP8 indexer cache 的稀疏 indexer）。ML4 特有的差异叠加在其上：共享 indexer 层复用最近的前一个 indexer 层的 top-k；indexer 拥有自己的 SSMax；NoPE 层上使用 NoPE indexer。每个 token 的 KV cache 存储 47,136 字节：41,328 字节用于 MLA latent，5,808 字节用于 indexer。
跨层 KV 共享。 九个 NoPE 层读取第 35 层写入的 latent KV，而不是写入自己的 KV。我们在 kv_sharing_target_layer_name 到 MLAAttention 以及 AttentionLayerBase 中加入了支持。消费层跳过 cache 写入，V2 runner 将它们解析为目标层的 KV cache 规格。消费层不占用 KV 内存：72 层中有 63 层拥有自己的 cache。 该特性与模型无关，正在 vllm#64095 中向上游合入。
NoPE、SSMax 与 LeRoPE。 NoPE 层以 RoPE 维度为零的 MLA 形式表达，因此使用相同的 kernel 和 cache 布局。LeRoPE 被折叠进 YaRN 频率。SSMax 被融合进 MLA RoPE kernel（见下文融合部分）。

items.title: OpenRouter 教程：用 LLM 从 PDF 中抽取表格
items.description: OpenRouter 发布教程，讲解如何把 PDF 以文件形式连同严格 JSON schema 发给能读文件的模型，让表格以带类型的行返回，括号亏损、千分位和脚注标记等清理都写进字段描述。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/l928e49lwysm0ymgmhyjrkc3z
items.excerpt:
How to Extract Tables from a PDF with an LLM
OpenRouter 发布教程，讲解如何把 PDF 以文件形式连同严格 JSON schema 发给能读文件的模型，让表格以带类型的行返回，括号亏损、千分位和脚注标记等清理都写进字段描述。
OpenRouter 用五份 PDF 实测了多条抽取路由，给出严格 JSON schema 写法、两类静默失败的检查和各路由成本对比。
要用 LLM 从 PDF 中提取表格，先把 PDF 发给 能读取文件的模型 ，同时附上一份 严格的 JSON schema ，用它描述表格中的一行。模型会返回带类型的行：数量以整数返回，写成 (3,878) 的亏损返回 -3878，跨两页的表格则返回成一个列表。
我们在五份 PDF 上做了测试，其中两份是扫描件。所有直接读取 PDF 的模型都把 644 个单元格全部答对。测试中的失败都出在 PDF 到达模型所走的路径上，其中两次还返回了正常响应、没有报错。
代码对数字版 PDF 和扫描件都能用，但结果取决于 PDF 是否带文本层、扫描质量、解析路径和模型。示例用了五份测试 PDF，它们都由已知数据生成，因此每个单元格都能与源数据核对。这五份分别是：一张发票、一份季度报告、一份 58 行、跨到第二页的出货记录、一份扫描的采购订单，以及一份故意做得很粗糙、带合并单元格的扫描件。
把下面的代码保存为 extract_tables.py 。它把 PDF 作为文件内容部分发送（做法见我们的 PDF 输入 页面），并通过 结构化输出 要求返回符合你 schema 的 JSON。把 strict 设为 true 后，支持严格模式的提供商会让输出严格遵循 schema，于是每一行都包含全部字段且类型正确。各提供商的支持情况不一，结构化输出页面说明了如何只路由到支持该功能的提供商。
return 之前的两个检查用来捕获第 3 步和第 4 步中提到的失败情况，请保留它们。费用来自 usage.cost ， 用量统计 会在每个响应中给出。
这次调用耗时约六秒。PDF 上显示的是 6,067.00，而返回的行里是 6067.0，这个数字不用先清理就能直接相加。去掉千位分隔符的正是字段描述。
PDF 表格所需的大部分清理工作都可以写进 schema 的字段描述里。我们的季度报告中有一个“Fiscal 2026”表头，横跨四个季度列；亏损用括号表示；还有两个业务板块名称（Enterprise 和 Hardware resale）带脚注标记。字段描述负责处理括号和脚注标记。跨列表头不需要描述，因为字段名已经说明了每个值属于哪个季度。
在“硬件转售”这一行里，(3,878) 返回成了 -3878，而且两个片段名称里的脚注标记都不见了。
纵向合并的单元格也是同样的道理。在我们粗略的扫描中，每个 Category 单元格跨六到九行。我们对这个字段的描述是：“第一列中的类别。它是合并单元格，因此要在它覆盖的每一行上重复填写。”在我们的测试中，这一句说明就足以让三个能读 PDF 的模型在全部 30 行上都填好类别。
如果模型能读文件，我们就把 PDF 直接交给它。如果模型不能读文件，我们先解析 PDF，再把结果发给模型。文件解析器插件的 engine 设置决定用哪个解析器。在不能读文件的模型上不设置它时，我们会使用 mistral-ocr ，正如 PDF 输入 页面所述。根据你的 PDF 长什么样来选择路线。
下面是把扫描版采购订单分别交给各解析器后、再发给 deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash 的结果。该模型接受图片但不接受文件，所以 PDF 必须先经过解析器。
这个 ValueError 来自第 1 步的空行检查。没有这项检查，第二次调用会返回 200 OK，同时给出 finish_reason: "stop" 和 {"rows": []} 。解析器在扫描件上没找到文字，模型也正确地报告了空表格。整个过程不会抛出任何错误，所以没有这项检查的流水线会存入零行数据，然后继续处理下一个文件。这是两种静默失败中的第一种。我们的粗略扫描表现相同，30 行里得了 0 分。
原生引擎只适用于能读文件的模型。当我们还是在 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 上设置了 engine="native" 时，请求成功了一次，随后两次因提供商错误而失败。
在同一个模型上不设置 engine 时，我们试了两次都正常，所以不要在不能读文件的模型上设置 native 。
模型写出的每一行都要消耗输出 token，所以长表格需要较高的 max_tokens 。我们那份 58 行的发货日志根据模型不同，用了 2,500 到 7,700 个输出 token，这让最啰嗦的模型在 extract_table 默认的 8,000 之下几乎没有余量。折算下来是每行 43 到 133 个 token。对于长表格，可以按每个预期行约 150 个 token 起步。然后测量你自己数据的每行用量，并保留 finish_reason 检查，因为具体数量会因模型和 schema 而异。下面是上限设得太低时会发生的情况。
没有 finish_reason 检查时，这个请求会以两种方式之一失败。普通 JSON 解析会在被截断的数组上抛出错误。
第二种方式就是另一种静默失败。开启 Response Healing 插件后，JSON 能解析，你会得到 58 行中的 5 行，且不抛异常。Healing 修复的是输出的语法，而它的文档警告说，它无法恢复被 max_tokens 截断的输出，所以它补不出模型根本没写的那些行。 finish_reason 检查能同时抓住这两种情况。
每一行都带有 schema 中定义的键，因此 csv.DictWriter 可以直接从 schema 取列名，并按原样写入各行。Excel 能直接打开结果文件。
表格延伸到了第二页，表头也在那里重复出现

Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson on building the backend for AI agents
I first met Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson in Singapore, shortly after they finished YC as the hottest startup of YC S20 . Six years later, we finally got them on the podcast! This is their first podcast together, after taking an open-source, fully remote company from zero to a $10 billion valuation.
The title is a question I wanted to understand for myself: why do agents love Supabase? There are plenty of managed databases. Postgres hosting is competitive. Being familiar to a model is useful distribution, but it doesn't explain all the work needed to turn a generated application into something that runs. But when I ran my frontier AEO tracker , it was an almost complete sweep of first choice for app backends (and in contention for managed db ) for every frontier model from Astra to Fable to Muse.
At Select, Supabase grouped its announcements into Build, Operate and Scale.
The things that stood out to me were surprisingly practical: start a local backend without Docker, keep the desired database schema in Git, and run compute beside the database. Each removes a piece of work that developers have been doing for years. Agents make that friction harder to ignore.
Watch the full conversation, including my opening commentary →
My favorite developer-tool announcements make me think: of course I want this today. The new alpha runtime for running Supabase locally without Docker is one of those. I use Colima rather than Docker Desktop, and even then, removing another dependency from the path to a working database is welcome. Local setup is a small part of a human developer's week; an agent that repeatedly creates and tests environments encounters it over and over.
Declarative schemas are the bigger idea. The familiar SQL workflow accumulates a history: create the schema, then migrate, migrate, migrate. A declarative representation gives the agent a description of the state you want, in files it can inspect and edit alongside the application.

items.title: Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing
items.description: Faraday Future is best known as an electric vehicle company, but it is increasingly positioning robotics as a major part of its future, describing itself more broadly as a “physical AI ecosystem company”. The California-based company is now trying to build a US robotics business around technology and products that currently rely substantially on Chinese […]
items.excerpt:
Faraday Future is best known as an electric vehicle company, but it is increasingly positioning robotics as a major part of its future, describing itself more broadly as a “physical AI ecosystem company”.
The California-based company is now trying to build a US robotics business around technology and products that currently rely substantially on Chinese manufacturing partners.
At its recent “Built in USA” conference in Los Angeles, FF outlined plans to bring a US robot factory online by the end of 2026, with its first US-assembled robot scheduled for February 2027.
The company ultimately wants to move beyond domestic assembly towards greater US manufacturing, while introducing three to five new or next-generation robotics products in the country each year.
That strategy comes at an interesting time. Chinese manufacturers have established a commanding position in the rapidly growing humanoid robotics market, while US regulators are paying increasing attention to foreign-made connected technologies and their supply chains.
For FF, therefore, bringing robotics production to the US is about more than simply moving an assembly line. The company sees localization as a way to strengthen regulatory compliance, supply-chain resilience, quality control and customer support while gradually developing domestic suppliers and manufacturing capabilities.
In this interview with Robotics & Automation News , Jerry Wang , global executive chairman of Faraday Future, explains how the company intends to make that transition and why it believes its experience in electric vehicles gives it a useful starting point.
Wang discusses the implications of new FCC rules, the likely cost disadvantage of manufacturing robots in the US and the challenges involved in replacing imported components with domestically sourced alternatives.
He also explains how FF could reuse parts of its existing EV manufacturing infrastructure, including its Hanford, California factory, and argues that electric vehicles and robots are not simply two unrelated businesses.
Instead, Wang says technologies including AI, perception, sensor fusion, computing, connectivity and data can form a common foundation for both – with robotics potentially becoming a significant new growth business alongside FF’s automotive operations.

items.description: By Nathan Spitalny, CEO of RDE Technologies Walk through most small and mid-sized plants and you’ll find them: the Windows box running the HMI on line two, the SCADA workstation in the control room, the engineering laptop that only comes out when a PLC program needs changing. items.excerpt:
By Nathan Spitalny , CEO of RDE Technologies
Walk through most small and mid-sized plants and you’ll find them: the Windows box running the HMI on line two, the SCADA workstation in the control room, the engineering laptop that only comes out when a PLC program needs changing. They keep production moving, and they are often the least-watched computers in the building.
Office IT usually gets the attention. Laptops are patched, email is filtered, and someone is alerted when a server fills up. The plant-floor PCs are different. They were set up by an integrator, they “just work,” and nobody wants to touch them in case a reboot stops a line.
Remote monitoring and management, or RMM software , puts a small agent on each Windows machine and reports its health to one dashboard.
For plant-floor PCs, the useful checks are basic:
The key is configuration. On production machines, patching should be approved and timed around maintenance windows, and alerts should go to someone who understands that rebooting an HMI mid-shift is not an option.
RMM tools are powerful, and attackers know it. In 2023, CISA warned that criminals were using legitimate remote monitoring tools to gain access and avoid detection ( CISA advisory AA23-025A ).
So treat the RMM console like the keys to the plant: require multi-factor authentication, limit who can open remote sessions, log every session, and keep the agent off PLCs and safety systems entirely. RMM belongs on the Windows machines, not on the controllers themselves.
Begin with an inventory: list every Windows machine that touches production, its operating system and who supports it. Then put the most critical few under monitoring, agree patch windows with operations, and separate the plant network from the office.
None of this needs new robots or a big budget. It just means treating the computers behind automation with the same care as the ones on desks.

items.title: Design the Human-Machine System: Automation, Robotics, and Human-in-the-Loop
items.description: Automation is easy to admire in isolation. The harder question is what it does to the operating system around it. A robot, sorter, autonomous vehicle, optimization engine, or AI agent changes process flow, exception patterns, skills, maintenance, data, and decision rights at the same time. The post Design the Human-Machine System: Automation, Robotics, and Human-in-the-Loop appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Automation is easy to admire in isolation. The harder question is what it does to the operating system around it. A robot, sorter, autonomous vehicle, optimization engine, or AI agent changes process flow, exception patterns, skills, maintenance, data, and decision rights at the same time.
Those are legitimate questions, but they are not enough. Automation changes the operating system. It changes process flow, exception patterns, maintenance requirements, skills, decision rights, safety considerations, data needs, and the role of the people who remain. That makes automation a systems design problem. The AI-agents-in-logistics discussion makes this human-machine boundary operational: the key design question is not whether software can act, but which classes of action it should own under defined guardrails.
A familiar warning in technology projects is not to automate a bad process. In logistics networks, the warning deserves more attention because physical automation is expensive and relatively inflexible after deployment.
If a warehouse process contains unnecessary movement, unclear priorities, poor slotting, or unstable order-release logic, automation may simply lock those problems into equipment and software. If a transportation-approval workflow includes unnecessary handoffs, an AI agent can make the recommendation instantly and still wait in the same approval queue.
The first design question should be what the future process should look like. Only then should the organization determine which portions are best performed by people, conventional automation, robotics, optimization, or AI.
The objective is not to prove that one is better. Machines are excellent at repetition, speed, precision, scale, monitoring, and operating within defined rules. Humans remain strong at handling ambiguity, interpreting context, negotiating competing objectives, dealing with novel conditions, and recognizing when the system itself may be wrong. A mature automation design assigns work accordingly.
In a warehouse, robots may handle repetitive movement while people manage irregular items, exceptions, maintenance coordination, and flow balancing. In transportation, optimization may build the baseline plan while humans resolve capacity crises, commercial tradeoffs, and unusual service exceptions. In yards and docks, automation may sequence trailers while supervisors manage safety and disruptions. The operating model should make those boundaries clear.

For years, the industry prepared for quantum computing to rewrite the rules of cybersecurity. Then AI got there first.
This summer, OpenAI’s agents broke out of a cybersecurity evaluation and breached Hugging Face’s production systems. They exploited vulnerabilities, used stolen credentials, and worked their way into another company’s infrastructure, all to get the answers to their tests. OpenAI’s incident report describes how the models chained together the steps to get there.
This was just a preview. Since then, AI has helped uncover weaknesses in software that much of the internet depends on. Just last week, companies were scrambling to patch critical flaws in PHP , which powers roughly 70% of websites. The flaws had been sitting there for more than a decade before researchers working through OpenAI’s Patch the Planet initiative helped uncover them. That same day, eMudhra , a certificate authority trusted by every major browser, was found to have used encryption keys so weak that one of them was just the number 4.
Mistakes like that have always existed, but models are getting better at finding weaknesses and figuring out how to exploit them. The progress is visible in the AI Security Institute’s evaluations , where newer models can complete increasingly complex cyber tasks.
More serious vulnerabilities are also being reported . With the growing volume confronting companies, security teams have to determine which weaknesses pose the greatest risk to their business and get them fixed before someone exploits them.
Meanwhile, the environment they’re protecting keeps growing. Employees are shipping applications they couldn’t have built a year ago. Agents are getting access to company documents, source code, and production systems. Every new application and connection gives security another thing to understand and protect.
That helps explain why we’ve seen the market caps of cybersecurity platforms like Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike take off this year.
There is more to secure. And enterprise budgets are following.

I’ve written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents —the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we’ve reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it’s for vibe coding computer games .
Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game:
That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that looks like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments . The challenge has been getting to a game that’s actually fun to play .
Game design is a deep subject area. I won’t pretend to be well versed in it—I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn’t think the models could do it.
Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to “Make it a LOT more fun”... and it did .
In the past few weeks I’ve vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term —no looking at the code at all) four games that I’ve genuinely enjoyed playing.
I attended Foo Camp in Berkeley over the weekend and met several people who were having similar experiences. Building games that play well is shockingly easy now. The new challenge is coming up with concepts for games that are novel and delightful and that wouldn’t exist without AI assistance.
I haven’t done an exhaustive study, but my current impression is that GPT-6 Astra isn’t quite there yet. It can absolutely build a game, but its sense of fun doesn’t match that of Opus 5.5. I expect OpenAI will get there by the end of the year.
Here are the four game projects that have convinced me that the models are now capable of producing fun games with very little guidance. All four are built in HTML and JavaScript and run entirely in the browser.
The smallest game I found to be genuinely delightful is Tree Appreciator . I used the regular Claude chat interface for this—it didn’t even need Claude Code.
I built this on a whim while we were driving along Skyline Boulevard looking at trees. My prompt was:
Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful.

items.title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
items.description: A sort of review of the benchmarking industry and what's missing.
items.excerpt:
Hill-climbing is easy, knowing what to hill-climb is hard. Making scores go up is expensive , but we have a much clearer playbook for it than we do for creating meaningful benchmarks at the true frontier of AI today.
Independent evaluation of language models is under-appreciated in how hard of a task it is. These groups are not just taking current models and certifying their scores, which is a technically involved task. This is their job if AI progress is slow. When AI progress is as fast as it is, the technical details of the job are the routine work part of trying to put a single number on what makes for a good AI model today. The goal is to have a single number that is representative of current models, matching vibe checks, community sentiment, and scientific analysis, while being forward looking enough so that it’s not outdated in 3 months.
Everyone building a benchmark faces a sort of paradox. You need your benchmark to reduce to one single number, so that it is easy to discuss, use in reports, and compare models, but every method of aggregating scores comes with meaningful trade-offs. The best scientists need to do this, everyone does. It’s a matter of creating aggregation metrics that you think are most fair, knowing there will always be imperfections.
With the amount of money in the AI ecosystem today, the weight of independent evaluation is even higher – you dictate the winners and losers of a trillion dollar market. You also influence some of the models themselves, steering the shape of progress. This is a lot of pressure!
My prompt for this article is Artificial Analysis’s recent update to their Intelligence Index, v5 . The AA index is the most prominent independent intelligence metric for the latest frontier models, followed in a distant second by Epoch AI’s Capabilities Index (ECI) . To date, all of these have been incredibly useful for the community and massively flawed!

An autonomous UV-C disinfection robot developed by Ryberg Healthcare has met international disinfection standards, according to a study by researchers at Leiden University .
The Omnia robot was evaluated by researchers at the university’s Institute of Biology Leiden in a furnished laboratory designed to emulate a hospital environment.
Published in the peer-reviewed journal Infection Prevention in Practice , the study found that the autonomously moving robot met acceptance criteria requiring a log reduction of at least 5.
Researchers tested Omnia against several indicator bacteria and reported reductions of more than 7 log for Escherichia coli and more than 5 log for Pseudomonas putida, used as a model for the hospital pathogen P. aeruginosa.
On Omnia’s “Deep” setting, Bacillus subtilis, a model for Gram-positive bacteria, was reduced by more than 7 log.
Researchers also compared autonomous and static UV-C disinfection. They found that autonomous operation was more effective than a static device for the same disinfection duration and light intensity, particularly in partially shadowed areas.
In a static test conducted according to British standard BS 8628:2022, the robot achieved a 4.0 log reduction for E. coli, below the required 5 log threshold. With the robot moving autonomously, the reduction exceeded 7 log.
The authors conclude: “This study demonstrates that the robot is capable of achieving log reductions higher than currently used disinfection methods, and the disinfection reports generated provide an indication for actual microbial log reductions achieved.”
They also conclude that “UV-C disinfection with an autonomous robot is more effective than using a static device for the same disinfection duration and light intensity.”
The researchers stressed that autonomous UV-C disinfection is intended to supplement rather than replace manual cleaning.

items.description: The Future of TMS: From Transportation Planning to Intelligent Execution should not be read as a prediction that the current category disappears. The more likely future is that its core responsibilities remain while the operating model around them becomes more continuous, connected, intelligent, and… The post The Future of TMS: From Transportation Planning to Intelligent Execution appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
TMS is unlikely to disappear; its core responsibilities are more likely to expand into a more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous execution model. The category’s future is therefore less about replacement than about how transportation execution is re-architected around real-time state and decisions.
TMS is moving from periodic planning and transaction execution toward continuous transportation management, where plans are refreshed as orders, capacity, service risk, and operating constraints change That shift requires systems to understand not only what transaction was completed but what the current state means for the next decision. Events become inputs to a continuously refreshed operating model. That trajectory follows the discipline in Engineer AI Into the Decision : intelligent transportation execution requires optimization and AI to be connected to explicit decision rights and executable workflows.
AI will be most useful where it can assemble context, interpret unstructured information, identify patterns, generate options, and support repetitive multi-step work. Optimization, rules, and traditional algorithms remain essential where constraints and feasible tradeoffs are mathematically explicit. The strongest architectures will combine these methods rather than treating one model as universal.
Routine decisions involving a tender rejection, a late pickup, a new order after the plan is built, a capacity shortfall, a missed delivery window, or a warehouse constraint that makes the transportation plan infeasible can increasingly be prepared or executed automatically when policy, data confidence, financial exposure, and customer impact remain inside defined limits. Higher-consequence or ambiguous situations should continue to escalate to people. The design target is appropriate autonomy, not maximum autonomy.

items.excerpt:
There is a gap between what warehouse operators expect from automation and what they get, said Exotec SAS. The company today released “Avoid Robot Regret: What Separates Automation That Delivers From Automation That Disappoints,” based on a survey of 250 supply chain decision-makers across the U.S. and Canada.
According to the report, one in four supply chain leaders said they wish they had gone a different way with automation. However, once they made the decision, 94% said switching providers would be prohibitively expensive, leaving most buyers with the systems they chose for the next 10 to 15 years.
Founded in 2015, Exotec said it delivers “flexible, reliable end-to-end robotic solutions for modern fulfillment operations.” By designing and manufacturing its own technology and solutions, Wasquehal, France-based company said it serves as a single automation provider, reducing complexity and risk while accelerating time to value compared with traditional systems.
Larger budgets and bigger teams don’t prevent the problem of robot regret, said Exotec. Companies with more than $1 billion in revenue were more likely to say their most significant automation investment underperformed than those with less than $1 billion in revenue (21% vs. 13%).
Across the survey, regret traced back to three decisions made before implementation:
Underestimating lifetime cost: Sixty-five percent of leaders said the total cost of ownership (TCO) came in higher than expected. Seventy percent said undisclosed costs have raised their annual maintenance spend. Among respondents whose systems underperformed, 43% said total costs ran 26% to 100% above expectations.

Buyers that worked directly with the equipment manufacturers rated the speed of root-cause identification higher than other buyers (75% versus 69%).
Timing. More than a quarter (27%) said their operations were not ready when they invested in and implemented automation. Early adopters with dedicated automation teams and leadership oversight rarely regretted their choice: One percent said they picked the wrong vendors, compared with 11% of fast followers.

“The RGF is about creating a world people can build, compete in, and belong to,” said D’Arcangelo. “Human ingenuity creates the technology, the teams, and the traditions. Robot sports give that creativity a new arena.”

items.title: Super El Niño: Supply Chain Risks
items.description: Food and beverage market is most exposed, followed by fertilizers and chemicals says a new Everstream Analytics report.
items.excerpt:
The 2026–27 Super El Niño is expected to peak in November–December 2026 and keep disrupting weather patterns through at least the first half of 2027.
A new report from Everstream Analytics, offers an analysis of the risks as well as ways companies can increase their readiness.
Five things supply chain leaders need to know:
Risk has moved from the Atlantic to the Pacific The Atlantic hurricane season is the quietest on record, while East and West Pacific storm activity runs far above normal, hitting coastal China, Japan, the Koreas and the Philippines.
Southeast Asia is ground zero Drought in Indonesia is driving wildfires, haze, aviation disruption, low rivers and the worst palm crop conditions in at least 10 years. Europe's waterways remain constrained Rhine gauges at Kaub and Cologne sit at record lows, keeping draft restrictions and higher freight costs in place through October. The Panama Canal faces continued restrictions Gatun Lake is below average but better than in past El Niño years, thanks to early water management. Food and beverage is most exposed Fertilizers, chemicals, energy, electronics, industrial manufacturing and apparel follow.
The report advises companies to use the following steps to mitigate the risk.
Map suppliers, sites and sub-tier sources in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and India; assess drought, wildfire and haze exposure through Q1 2027.
Secure alternative or buffer supply for palm oil and other Southeast Asian tropical crops before yield losses reach pricing.
Stress-test West Pacific port and shipping plans for continued typhoon disruption.
Plan around Rhine draft limits through October, then prepare for flooding in France, Spain and Italy as Europe turns wetter.
Budget for Panama Canal draft limits through December–February and evaluate alternative routings.
Add Australia, northern South America and Central America to active dryness monitoring.
Build 2027 plans for a normal to slightly above normal Atlantic hurricane season.

items.title: How Anthropic ships Claude with Claude: Separating the Brain from the Hands
items.description: Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang on Opus 5.5, the Claude Platform, and the engineering behind AI agents.
items.excerpt:
Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang on Opus 5.5, the Claude Platform, and the engineering behind AI agents.
As we learned from the Anthropic S-1 filings yesterday , the lab has some of the highest revenue and research efficiency in human history, particularly with -126% loss to 19% GAAP profit turnaround in the last year. The company credits this to their two core loops: Improvement and Investment:
Today we go inside how Anthropic works. Now the dust has settled on Opus 5.5 and it has lasted a month as the generally accepted #1 LLM in the world, we dive into its launch, and how Anthropic ships Claude with Claude with Katelyn Lesse and Angela Jiang , heads of Engineering and Product respectively.
The team is working under two kinds of pressure. The models are getting more capable, which makes safe deployment and access decisions harder. At the same time, usage is growing fast enough that ordinary infrastructure choices—like how much CPU an API consumes—become strategic. Those problems meet in the product choices that reach developers.
Anthropic's Opus 5.5 launch emphasizes both model quality and cost. We discuss feedback that the previous Opus generations were be too verbose, alongside the need for stronger intelligence per dollar. Anthropic says the new model costs less to run than its predecessor; the exact saving depends on the workload and its use of cached context.
The less visible launch work involves changes to how people integrate the API. One example we discuss is protecting model reasoning against extraction used for distillation. Preserving thinking blocks across turns helps address this, but a new requirement can also break a customer's existing harness.
Katelyn also describes what being part of early access programs actually looks like in practice: Customers run evaluations in their own harnesses, report surprising behavior, and sometimes pass along less formal impressions. The useful part is not just a benchmark score: it is seeing the model in environments and tasks Anthropic's own products do not cover. As we have said for 4 straight years now on the podcast , having good evals is golden.
Our favorite mental model in the episode is the distinction between an agent's brain and its hands. In Managed Agents , Anthropic separates the session log and harness from the sandbox that executes code. The harness can persist while an execution environment is created when needed; a failed sandbox does not have to take the whole agent session with it.

items.title: Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next
items.description: Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next should not be read as a prediction that the current category disappears. The more likely future is that its core responsibilities remain while the operating model around them becomes more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous. The post Beyond WMS: Where Warehouse Execution Is Headed Next appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
WMS is unlikely to disappear; its core responsibilities are more likely to expand into a more continuous, connected, intelligent, and selectively autonomous execution model. The category’s future is therefore less about replacement than about how warehouse execution is re-architected around real-time state and decisions.
WMS is moving from a transactional warehouse application toward a real-time execution and orchestration layer that coordinates inventory, labor, automation, and downstream transportation constraints That shift requires systems to understand not only what transaction was completed but what the current state means for the next decision. Events become inputs to a continuously refreshed operating model. The future of warehouse execution will therefore depend on the human-machine allocation described in Design the Human-Machine System : automation should expand where authority, observability, and recovery are engineered well enough to support it.
AI will be most useful where it can assemble context, interpret unstructured information, identify patterns, generate options, and support repetitive multi-step work. Optimization, rules, and traditional algorithms remain essential where constraints and feasible tradeoffs are mathematically explicit. The strongest architectures will combine these methods rather than treating one model as universal.
Routine decisions involving a late inbound trailer, a constrained dock, a wave that threatens a carrier cutoff, an automation cell that goes down, or an urgent order that must be reprioritized without destabilizing the rest of the facility can increasingly be prepared or executed automatically when policy, data confidence, financial exposure, and customer impact remain inside defined limits. Higher-consequence or ambiguous situations should continue to escalate to people. The design target is appropriate autonomy, not maximum autonomy.
As software gains more authority, decision rights have to be encoded in permissions, thresholds, workflow states, escalation paths, and audit trails. A platform should be able to reconstruct what it knew, what it recommended or changed, under whose authority, and with what result.

LFM3 is our new generation of Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs), built to be the starting point for specialized intelligence. It brings text, vision, audio, omni, and decision models onto one shared backbone, all in the 2B parameter range. This means you can pick the model for your modality, fine-tune it on your own data on a single GPU, and deploy it where your application runs.
LFM3 brings four main changes compared to our previous LFM2 family:
LFM2 showed that a hybrid of short convolutions and attention can run fast on-device without sacrificing quality. For LFM3, we used our hardware-in-the-loop architecture search to redesign that architecture for agentic use cases, which need more capability per parameter and fast inference over long contexts. The search now covers 14 device and backend combinations, from phones and a Raspberry Pi 5 to laptops, cloud CPUs, GPUs, and the Qualcomm Hexagon NPU.

The payoff shows at long context. Per parameter, LFM3-1.7B matches LFM2-1.2B on short prompts across edge devices, and with 8K tokens in context it is about 25% faster. LFM3-1.7B-Base was pre-trained on 22T tokens with the same 128K vocabulary as LFM2.5-8B-A1B . The final 3.5T tokens are a mid-training stage on curated data with a larger share of agentic traces and tool calls, which also extends the context window to 256K tokens.
Every LFM3 model branches from LFM3-1.7B-Base. Instead of running one large general-purpose model, you pick the one that fits your inputs, customize it, and run it on-device.
